chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, both together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a sheikh from our companions known as Abu al-Hasan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and High, created a white rooster, its neck is beneath the Throne, and its feet are at the edges of the seventh earth. It has a wing in the East and a wing in the West. The roosters do not crow until it crows. So whenever it crows, it flaps its wings, then says: 'Glory be to Allah! Glory be to Allah the Magnificent, Who does not resemble anything.' He said: So Allah, Blessed and High, answers it, saying: 'He would not swear by Me falsely, the one who recognizes what you are saying.'

key_terms.تُخُومِ الْأَرْضِ السَّابِعَةِ: The edges of the seventh earth

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the cosmic rooster in Shia cosmology?
ai.summary: In the context of validating oaths, this hadith from Al-Kafi introduces a cosmic rooster whose preeminent crowing serves as a divine witness to truthfulness, reinforcing the gravity of swearing by Allah. The narrative highlights the metaphysical hierarchy where this creature's glorification elicits a direct response from Allah, affirming that those who know the reality of His name do not lie. This imagery underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible spiritual presence of divine attributes in the unseen world.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, both together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed, from a sheykh from our companions with a teknonym of Abu Al Hassan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Created a white rooster, its neck is beneath the Throne, and its feet as in the edge of the seventh firmament. For it is a wing in the east and a wing in the west. The roosters (of the world) do not shriek until it shrieks. So whenever it shrieks, it flaps with its wings, then says: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Glory be to Allah<sup>saww</sup> the Magnificent, Who does not resemble anything’. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Answers it, so He<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying: “He would not swear by Me<sup>azwj</sup> falsely, the one who recognises what you are saying”.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali has narrated from his father from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from a Shaykh of our people called abu al-Hassan who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Allah, most Blessed, most High, has created a white rooster whose neck is under the throne and its legs in the center of the seventh earth, its one wing is in the east and one wing in the west. Other roosters do not crow until it crows. When it wants to crow it flaps its wings and says, ‘Tasbih (Allah is free of all defects) and is the most great like whom there is no one.’” He (the Imam) said that ‘Allah, most Blessed, most High, in response says, “A lying person would never swear falsely by My name would he but know about what you say.’””
